name: macOS Forensic Artifacts
description: Extraction and analysis of macOS-specific forensic artifacts. Covers Unified Logging (log show/log collect), FSEvents for file system activity reconstruction, Spotlight metadata (mdls, mdfind), KnowledgeC database (and the Biome streams that increasingly supersede it on recent macOS versions) for application and device usage, TCC.db for privacy permission history, quarantine events and XProtect detections, Apple Mail and iMessage artifact analysis, Safari history and downloads, Launch Services database, and APFS snapshot forensics.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to macOS forensic artifact analysis

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands macOS artifact categories and their forensic value
evidence: Can describe major macOS artifact sources (Unified Logs, FSEvents, Spotlight, KnowledgeC)
Understands APFS filesystem structure and its forensic implications
Familiar with macOS-specific artifact locations compared to Windows/Linux equivalents
Completed introductory training on macOS forensics

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Extracts and parses macOS artifacts under supervision
evidence: Collected and filtered Unified Logs using log collect/log show (including offline .logarchive parsing from disk images) under guidance
Parsed FSEvents databases to reconstruct file system activity
Extracted Spotlight metadata and quarantine event records
Analysed Safari history, downloads, and bookmark artifacts with supervisor review

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently analyses macOS artifacts across investigation types
evidence: Independently analysed macOS artifacts in 5+ investigations
Correlates KnowledgeC, FSEvents, and Unified Logs to reconstruct user activity timelines
Extracts and interprets TCC.db permission grants and quarantine attributes
Produces macOS forensic reports withstanding peer and legal review

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles advanced macOS forensic scenarios; detects anti-forensics
evidence: Identifies evidence of macOS anti-forensic techniques (log clearing, FSEvents manipulation, timestomping)
Analyses APFS snapshots and Time Machine backups for historical state recovery
Develops custom parsers for macOS artifacts from new OS versions
Reviews and mentors junior examiners on macOS artifact analysis

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Authority on macOS forensics; discovers new artifact sources
evidence: Authored or maintains lab's macOS forensic analysis procedures
Published research on newly discovered macOS artifacts or analysis techniques
Validated forensic tool accuracy against macOS ground truth data
Provides expert testimony on macOS forensic evidence

assessment_methods.description: Given a macOS disk image, extract and analyze platform-specific artifacts to reconstruct user activity and determine program execution within a specified timeframe
Review macOS artifact analysis sections from recent case reports
